tier_reason: First-party README table (Performance section) times the twelve test/bench scripts under prolua and the installed Lua 5.4.8 with the public harness src/cli/bench.zig (whole process, best of 3, stdout ignored) and states Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseFast, but gives no CPU model and no build flags for the reference lua, so not A; no independent or peer-reviewed measurement, so not B.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig 0.16.0, zig build bench -Doptimize=ReleaseFast (runs prolua bench --dir test/bench); the measured 'installed' Lua 5.4.8 build is not described in the Performance section. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) builds the reference from the lua.org 5.4.8 tarball with 'make linux' (upstream Makefile defaults), and the README notes Ubuntu ships only 5.4.6, so a tarball build is likely but not stated for the benchmark run.
corrections.workload: Twelve scripts in test/bench (binarytrees, closures, coroutines, fannkuch, fib, json, loops, nbody, sort, spectralnorm, strings, tables), each timed as a whole process by src/cli/bench.zig (wall clock, best of three runs, child stdout discarded, non-zero exit fails the run), prolua run vs the reference lua found on PATH, measured 2026-09-12 on Linux.
corrections.caveats: Mixed result, not a uniform speed-up: faster on 4 of 12 scripts (sort 0.60x, loops 0.72x, coroutines 0.82x, nbody 0.89x), within 3% on 5, slower on 3 (json 1.15x, spectralnorm 1.19x, strings 1.19x). Whole-process times include interpreter start-up (fib runs only about 0.055 s). CPU model not given (only 'Linux'); the benchmarked reference Lua's build flags are not stated (CI builds it from the tarball with upstream defaults). The bench harness discards output and does not compare it, although the separate differential suite (55 scripts) and the official Lua 5.4.8 suite check semantics byte for byte. README calls it 'a very early release' not for production; repository created 2026-09-16 with three commits, 3 stars.

notes: README Performance table matches the record's numbers exactly; bench harness src/cli/bench.zig is a straightforward best-of-3 wall-clock runner against lua on PATH. Shortcomings to record: mixed result (wins 4 of 12, loses 3), no CPU model, reference Lua build flags unstated for the measured run, start-up included, very new 3-star repo.

tier_reason: First-party README 'Same-machine pair' gives Octane 2586 vs 2418 and microbench 3603 vs 4248 ns for the Zig port vs the C original, run via zig build octane / microbench (build.zig), but the C original's build flags, CPU model and run count are not stated, and the Octane driver tests/octane/run.js comes from the external mquickjs-extras tarball rather than the repo.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Octane score 2586 vs 2418 for the original C mquickjs (higher is better; about +7%, derived from page data); microbench 3603 vs 4248 ns per operation (about 15% less time, derived from page data). Single same-machine pair; the README says both numbers move with CPU load and Octane's Date.now() time budget.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: zig build octane / zig build microbench with -Doptimize=ReleaseFast. The numbers were committed on 2026-09-15 when debug-notes.md pinned Zig 0.16.0; the README now says Zig 0.17.0 after the 2026-10-05 migration and the numbers were not re-measured. Build flags of the C original (a local ../mquickjs/mqjs binary per debug-notes.md) are not stated; the upstream mquickjs Makefile defaults to CONFIG_SMALL=y, which compiles with -Os.
corrections.workload: Octane (tests/octane/run.js from Bellard's mquickjs-extras tarball, not included in the repo; zig build octane runs it with --memory-limit 256M) and the QuickJS microbenchmark tests/microbench.js (zig build microbench), each run once on the same machine for the C original and the Zig port.
corrections.caveats: Margin is small and within run-to-run noise: the C original scored about 2485 (debug-notes.md, August) and 2445 (earlier README) versus 2418 here, and the Zig port moved from 2536 to 2586 between two same-day commits. C build flags unstated; the upstream Makefile's default is -Os (CONFIG_SMALL=y), so a default C build would be size-optimized against Zig ReleaseFast. CPU model not stated. Until the 2026-09-15 'round 1' commit the port scored 1927 vs 2445 (README then said about 78% of C); most of the jump came from fixing a quadratic strstart scan in the port itself. The README warns the AI-assisted port has 'a ton of bugs that do not exist in the original' and must not be used where stability or security matter; it deviates from mquickjs (let/const aliased to var, eval always global) and reports 18.8% on test262 language tests (no figure for the C original, which is itself an ES5 subset). A deterministic fixed-iteration Octane differential in debug-notes.md produced identical state hashes on both engines for all 15 suites, so the Octane result does not come from skipped work. Port of bellard/mquickjs, which is already listed.

notes: README numbers match the record. Port of bellard/mquickjs (already verified in wave 12): orchestrator may fold it as a duplicate under the ports precedent, though it carries its own claim against the original. Shortcomings to record: single noisy run pair with a margin smaller than the baseline's own run-to-run spread, C build flags unstated (upstream default -Os), no CPU model, Octane driver external, known AI-port bugs and semantic deviations, numbers predate the Zig 0.17 migration.
